overview.context: Changes now open on a guide: an agent walks the diff in reading order, chapter by chapter, beside the real code. It is written by a hidden, read-only run of the chat that made the change, and refreshes after every turn, commit, and push.
steps: Provider sessions can run `read-only` with their own tools, and a shared `HiddenAgentRunner` owns those throwaway runs.
Review diffs get stable hunk ids, start at their enclosing function, and link code that moved between files.
The server outlines the change, then the agent writes chapters through checked `guide_*` tools that answer with what was kept or rejected.
Guides are stored per workspace, refreshed incrementally, and shown as Overview, Guide, and Diff in the Changes tab.

beforeAfter.caption: How a change reaches the reviewer

lines.code: show every file in folder order

chapters.title: Sessions carry their own tools
paragraphs: The MCP gateway learns `AppToolset`: a set of tool definitions plus a `call` handler that a single session brings with it. `SessionTools` replaces the old `orchestrationTools` argument everywhere a provider session starts, so orchestration and feature toolsets travel the same way.
Every driver passes `sessionTools` straight through to the gateway; none of them needed to learn what a guide is.
hints: Why thread tools through start() instead of a registry keyed by session?

chapters.title: A read-only policy for hidden runs
paragraphs: `StartSessionInput.toolPolicy: "read-only"` marks a session nobody is watching. Claude hides write tools entirely and allows only plain reads plus the session's own tools; Codex gets plan mode's access (no approvals, read-only sandbox) without plan mode's collaboration style.
`ProviderService` is the safety net: a read-only session's permission requests are denied without ever reaching the user, and its questions are dropped before they reach the question tray.
hints: Why deny silently instead of asking the user?

chapters.title: One runner for throwaway sessions
paragraphs: `HiddenAgentRunner.run` starts a session, hands its single turn's events to the caller, and closes the session however the run ends, including timeouts and interruption. An idle timeout catches a provider that stops talking.
Chat naming moves onto the same runner, so there is one place that owns hidden sessions' lifecycle.

chapters.title: Hunks get stable ids
paragraphs: `review-outline.ts` is the shared, pure model of a review diff. A hunk's id comes from its changed lines only, so it survives edits elsewhere in the file; that is what lets a guide recognize its chapters after the agent keeps working.
It also classifies files (core, tests, generated), spots whitespace- and import-only edits, and detects blocks moved between files. Its hash is the one `fnv1a` every client shares.

chapters.title: Diffs start where the function does
paragraphs: The `git.reviewPatches` handler extends each hunk upward to its enclosing function, using tree-sitter symbols for JS and TS and indentation elsewhere, so a one-line change arrives with its context. A hunk is only extended when the file on disk still matches it.
In Changes, hunks can now expand into the unchanged lines around them, reading the file once through the same loader the editor uses, and moved code shows linked chips at both ends.
hints: What happens to a hunk on a staged diff?

chapters.title: The guide's shape and storage
paragraphs: A guide is an overview (title, context, steps, and a before/after sketch whose lines cite chapters) plus chapters that own hunk ids. Runs stream as `ReviewGuideRun`; the stored `ReviewGuide` only changes when a run finishes.
Migration `0092` stores one guide per workspace with its chapters, and two settings turn guides and automatic refresh on or off.

chapters.title: The server outlines before the agent writes
paragraphs: `buildOutline` turns the change into handles like `h12` with a one-line digest each, and sets tests, generated files, and mechanical edits aside before any token is spent. Very large changes switch to one line per file.
The prompt carries the chat's own requests and last reply, plus PR text when there is one, as tagged data rather than instructions.
hints: Why outline on the server instead of letting the agent explore?

chapters.title: Chapters arrive through checked tools
paragraphs: The agent writes with four tools: `guide_read_hunks`, `guide_add_chapter`, `guide_set_overview`, and `guide_finish`. Every call is validated the moment it arrives and answers with what was kept, what was rejected and why, and what is still unplaced, so the agent fixes its own mistakes mid-run.
`guide_finish` refuses once while core hunks are unplaced, then gathers the rest under "Other changes".

chapters.title: Guides stay current on their own
paragraphs: `ReviewGuideService` runs one write per workspace, supersedes older runs, and swaps the finished guide in whole. A refresh keeps every chapter whose hunks are unchanged and asks the agent only about what moved; a run that writes nothing keeps the old guide and shows why.
Finished turns (through a new reactor), commits, and pushes ask for a refresh, debounced per workspace.
hints: Why skip turns that settled more than ten minutes ago?

chapters.title: Overview, Guide, and Diff in Changes
paragraphs: Changes gains three views behind a floating tab bar. The overview reads like a pull request page with the before/after sketch and chapter cards; the guide walks each chapter with its own hunks beside it; Diff is the familiar file-by-file review.
Reviewed state is the same per-file state everywhere, so checking a chapter checks its files.

diff --git a/apps/server/test/unit/scope-context.test.ts b/apps/server/test/unit/scope-context.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..215a3b4e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/server/test/unit/scope-context.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+import {
+	type FolderId,
+	GitDiffResult,
+	GitReviewFileContents,
+	GitReviewPatch,
+} from "@zuse/contracts";
+import type { GitService } from "@zuse/git/git-service";
+import { Effect } from "effect";
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+
+import {
+	extendReviewPatch,
+	fileScopesFrom,
+	innermostSymbol,
+} from "../../src/review/scope-context.ts";
+
+const source = [
+	"export class Cart {", // 1
+	"  total(items) {", // 2
+	"    let sum = 0;",
+	"    for (const item of items) {",
+	"      const price = item.price;",
+	"      const qty = item.qty;",
+	"      sum += price * qty;", // 7
+	"    }",
+	"    return sum;",
+	"  }",
+	"}",
+].join("\n");
+
+const symbols = [
+	{ name: "Cart", kind: "class", startLine: 1, endLine: 11 },
+	{ name: "total", kind: "method", startLine: 2, endLine: 10 },
+];
+
+const patchText = [
+	"diff --git a/cart.ts b/cart.ts",
+	"--- a/cart.ts",
+	"+++ b/cart.ts",
+	"@@ -5,3 +5,3 @@",
+	"       const price = item.price;",
+	"       const qty = item.qty;",
+	"-      sum += price;",
+	"+      sum += price * qty;",
+	"",
+].join("\n");
+
+const reviewPatch = (mode: "worktree" | "deleted" = "worktree") =>
+	GitReviewPatch.make({
+		path: "cart.ts",
+		error: null,
+		result: GitDiffResult.make({
+			mode,
+			patch: patchText,
+			truncated: false,
+			bytes: patchText.length,
+		}),
+	});
+
+const fakeGit = (newContent: string | null) =>
+	({
+		reviewFileContents: () =>
+			Effect.succeed(
+				GitReviewFileContents.make({
+					oldContent: null,
+					newContent,
+					mtime: "1",
+				}),
+			),
+	}) as unknown as GitService["Service"];
+
+describe("scope context", () => {
+	it("picks the innermost enclosing symbol", () => {
+		expect(innermostSymbol(symbols, 7)?.name).toBe("total");
+		expect(innermostSymbol(symbols, 1)?.name).toBe("Cart");
+		expect(innermostSymbol(symbols, 20)).toBeNull();
+	});
+
+	it("starts a scope at the symbol, falling back to indentation", () => {
+		expect(fileScopesFrom(source, symbols).startOf(7)).toBe(2);
+		expect(fileScopesFrom(source, []).startOf(7)).toBe(2);
+	});
+
+	it("extends a working-tree patch to its function", async () => {
+		const extended = await Effect.runPromise(
+			extendReviewPatch(
+				fakeGit(source),
+				"folder" as FolderId,
+				null,
+				"branch",
+				reviewPatch(),
+			),
+		);
+		expect(extended.result.patch).toContain("@@ -2,6 +2,6 @@");
+		expect(extended.result.patch).toContain("   total(items) {");
+		expect(extended.result.bytes).toBe(extended.result.patch.length);
+	});
+
+	it("leaves staged, deleted, and unreadable patches as git produced them", async () => {
+		const original = reviewPatch();
+		const staged = await Effect.runPromise(
+			extendReviewPatch(
+				fakeGit(source),
+				"f" as FolderId,
+				null,
+				"staged",
+				original,
+			),
+		);
+		expect(staged).toBe(original);
+		const deleted = reviewPatch("deleted");
+		expect(
+			await Effect.runPromise(
+				extendReviewPatch(
+					fakeGit(source),
+					"f" as FolderId,
+					null,
+					"branch",
+					deleted,
+				),
+			),
+		).toBe(deleted);
+		expect(
+			await Effect.runPromise(
+				extendReviewPatch(
+					fakeGit(null),
+					"f" as FolderId,
+					null,
+					"branch",
+					original,
+				),
+			),
+		).toBe(original);
+		const failing = {
+			reviewFileContents: () => Effect.fail(new Error("gone")),
+		} as unknown as GitService["Service"];
+		expect(
+			await Effect.runPromise(
+				extendReviewPatch(failing, "f" as FolderId, null, "branch", original),
+			),
+		).toBe(original);
+	});
+});

diff --git a/packages/contracts/src/review-guide.ts b/packages/contracts/src/review-guide.ts
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..0b62e05a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/contracts/src/review-guide.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+import { Schema } from "effect";
+import { Rpc } from "effect/unstable/rpc";
+
+import { ProviderId } from "./agent.ts";
+import { FolderId, WorktreeId } from "./ids.ts";
+import { SessionId } from "./session.ts";
+
+/**
+ * A guided review walks a reader through a workspace's changes in reading
+ * order, beside the diff itself: a before/after for the whole change, then
+ * short chapters, each owning the hunks that carry one idea. Tests,
+ * generated files, and mechanical edits (moves, renames, re-indentation)
+ * are grouped at the end, collapsed, so the reader starts where judgment is
+ * needed.
+ *
+ * Chapters own hunks by id (`path@fingerprint`, see `hunkIds` in
+ * `@zuse/client-runtime/review-outline`), so a guide written for one
+ * revision still recognizes its chapters after unrelated edits elsewhere.
+ */
+
+export const ReviewGuideChapterKind = Schema.Literals([
+	"core",
+	"tests",
+	"generated",
+	"mechanical",
+]);
+export type ReviewGuideChapterKind = typeof ReviewGuideChapterKind.Type;
+
+export class ReviewGuideChapter extends Schema.Class<ReviewGuideChapter>(
+	"ReviewGuideChapter",
+)({
+	id: Schema.String,
+	ordinal: Schema.Number,
+	kind: ReviewGuideChapterKind,
+	title: Schema.String,
+	/** Two or three sentences: what changed here and why it matters. */
+	summary: Schema.String,
+	hunkIds: Schema.Array(Schema.String),
+	/** Test hunks that exercise this chapter's code. */
+	validatedBy: Schema.Array(Schema.String),
+	/** Short questions a reader might ask the author about this chapter. */
+	askHints: Schema.Array(Schema.String),
+	/** Written by the server's classification rather than the agent. */
+	auto: Schema.Boolean,
+}) {}
+
+/**
+ * One line of the before/after sketch: a few lines of pseudo-code tracing the
+ * path the change touches. Removed lines are what used to happen, added lines
+ * what happens now, context lines what stayed. A changed line may carry a
+ * short note and the id of the chapter that implements it.
+ */
+export const ReviewGuideSketchLine = Schema.Struct({
+	kind: Schema.Literals(["context", "add", "remove"]),
+	indent: Schema.Number,
+	code: Schema.String,
+	note: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
+	chapterId: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
+});
+export type ReviewGuideSketchLine = typeof ReviewGuideSketchLine.Type;
+
+export class ReviewGuideOverview extends Schema.Class<ReviewGuideOverview>(
+	"ReviewGuideOverview",
+)({
+	/** A short title for the change, like a pull request's. */
+	title: Schema.String,
+	/** A sentence or two: what the change does and why. */
+	context: Schema.String,
+	/** Two to five steps the change takes, in the order it works. */
+	steps: Schema.Array(Schema.String),
+	beforeAfter: Schema.NullOr(
+		Schema.Struct({
+			/** What the sketch traces, e.g. "How a retry delay is chosen". */
+			caption: Schema.String,
+			lines: Schema.Array(ReviewGuideSketchLine),
+		}),
+	),
+}) {}
+
+export const ReviewGuideStatus = Schema.Literals([
+	"ready",
+	"failed",
+	"interrupted",
+]);
+export type ReviewGuideStatus = typeof ReviewGuideStatus.Type;
+
+export class ReviewGuide extends Schema.Class<ReviewGuide>("ReviewGuide")({
+	id: Schema.String,
+	folderId: FolderId,
+	worktreeId: Schema.NullOr(WorktreeId),
+	status: ReviewGuideStatus,
+	/** The chat whose agent wrote the code, and is the one to ask about it. */
+	originSessionId: Schema.NullOr(SessionId),
+	providerId: ProviderId,
+	model: Schema.String,
+	baseSha: Schema.String,
+	headSha: Schema.String,
+	overview: Schema.NullOr(ReviewGuideOverview),
+	chapters: Schema.Array(ReviewGuideChapter),
+	error: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
+	createdAt: Schema.Number,
+	updatedAt: Schema.Number,
+}) {}
+
+export class ReviewGuideRun extends Schema.Class<ReviewGuideRun>(
+	"ReviewGuideRun",
+)({
+	/** Short head the run is writing for, shown as "Updating for <sha>". */
+	forSha: Schema.String,
+	phase: Schema.Literals(["outlining", "writing"]),
+	overview: Schema.NullOr(ReviewGuideOverview),
+	/** Chapters written so far, in reading order. */
+	chapters: Schema.Array(ReviewGuideChapter),
+	assigned: Schema.Number,
+	total: Schema.Number,
+}) {}
+
+export const ReviewGuideUnavailableReason = Schema.Literals([
+	"disabled",
+	"unsupported-provider",
+	"no-session",
+	"no-changes",
+	"too-large",
+]);
+export type ReviewGuideUnavailableReason =
+	typeof ReviewGuideUnavailableReason.Type;
+
+export class ReviewGuideState extends Schema.Class<ReviewGuideState>(
+	"ReviewGuideState",
+)({
+	/** The last guide written, kept readable while a newer one is written. */
+	guide: Schema.NullOr(ReviewGuide),
+	run: Schema.NullOr(ReviewGuideRun),
+	/** Why a guide cannot be written right now, or null when it can. */
+	unavailable: Schema.NullOr(ReviewGuideUnavailableReason),
+	/** Why the last run failed, until the next one starts. */
+	lastError: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
+	/** Provider and model a new guide would be written with. */
+	writer: Schema.NullOr(
+		Schema.Struct({ providerId: ProviderId, model: Schema.String }),
+	),
+}) {}
+
+export class ReviewGuideError extends Schema.TaggedErrorClass<ReviewGuideError>()(
+	"ReviewGuideError",
+	{ reason: Schema.String },
+) {}
+
+const WorkspaceRef = {
+	folderId: FolderId,
+	worktreeId: Schema.NullOr(WorktreeId),
+};
+
+/** Live state of a workspace's guide: the stored one plus any run. */
+export const ReviewGuideStreamRpc = Rpc.make("reviewGuide.stream", {
+	payload: Schema.Struct(WorkspaceRef),
+	success: ReviewGuideState,
+	error: ReviewGuideError,
+	stream: true,
+});
+
+/**
+ * Write or refresh the guide now. `force` writes one even when the change is
+ * over the automatic size limit.
+ */
+export const ReviewGuideGenerateRpc = Rpc.make("reviewGuide.generate", {
+	payload: Schema.Struct({
+		...WorkspaceRef,
+		originSessionId: Schema.optional(Schema.NullOr(SessionId)),
+		force: Schema.optional(Schema.Boolean),
+	}),
+	success: Schema.Void,
+	error: ReviewGuideError,
+});
+
+export const ReviewGuideCancelRpc = Rpc.make("reviewGuide.cancel", {
+	payload: Schema.Struct(WorkspaceRef),
+	success: Schema.Void,
+	error: ReviewGuideError,
+});
